THING.description: root: any node type is-a THING

METHOD.description: a named modeling approach/theory/law/model (e.g. μ(I) rheology, kinetic theory, NGF, DEM, RFT)

PARAMETER.description: a named physical quantity/constant/coefficient in equations (e.g. μ, I, d, P, τ, g, ρ_s, T, A, ξ, μ_s, b)

PHENOMENON.description: a physical effect/behavior methods capture (e.g. nonlocal creep, thin-body strengthening, secondary rheology, segregation, clogging)

PROPERTY.description: a generic physical property/quantity not fitting the above (kept for residual cases)

constitutive_law.description: a constitutive law relating output quantity/quantities to >=1 input quantity (n-ary)
constitutive_law.semantic_boundary: a FORMAL/QUANTITATIVE law output=f(inputs+params), stated as a formula or explicit functional relation. NOT a prose 'X depends on Y' (that is influences), NOT a definition (defines), NOT a measurement setup (measures).

influences.description: one quantity influences / depends on >=1 target quantity (n-ary, general dependence)
influences.semantic_boundary: X functionally depends on / varies with Y (a genuine causal or scaling dependence). NOT a co-listing of parallel items (composed_of), NOT a classification (defines), NOT 'we tested X' (measures), NOT 'X is part of Y' (composed_of).

defines.description: one entity is defined-as / identified-with / named-by another (definitional identity, n-ary)
defines.semantic_boundary: a DEFINITIONAL identity: X is defined as / is / denotes / is named / is classified into Y. NOT a structural part-of (composed_of), NOT a functional dependence (influences). 'X is analogous to Y' is a CLAIM not a definition.

composed_of.description: one whole is composed-of / part-of >=1 component (n-ary composition)
composed_of.semantic_boundary: STRUCTURAL composition: parts that make up a whole (model A = B + C). NOT classification (defines), NOT 'X has control params' (influences), NOT experimental setup description, NOT 'we tested X by doing Y'.

measures.description: a quantity is measured by / characterizes >=1 measure
measures.semantic_boundary: a measurement/evaluation relation: X is measured/evaluated by instrument/method Y. NOT a functional law (constitutive_law), NOT a dependence (influences).

claim_relation.semantic_boundary: a DISCOURSE relation between claims/findings (supports/contrasts/outperforms). NOT a method-to-method development (extends/improves/compares — those are evolution), NOT a measurement (measures).

extends.semantic_boundary: X GENERALIZES Y (X extends Y's scope/regime/params; X is a direct technical extension of Y). NOT improves (X need not be more accurate, just broader), NOT background (X is a direct technical inheritance, not a motivation citation), NOT claim_relation (this is method-to-method).

improves.description: X improves Y's accuracy/applicability, resolving Y's limitation
improves.semantic_boundary: X RESOLVES a limitation of Y (X is more accurate/applicable BECAUSE it fixes something Y fails at; first-principles vs phenomenological = improves). NOT compares (X is NOT a parallel different-mechanism alternative; X builds on Y and is better), NOT extends (X is better not just broader).

compares.semantic_boundary: A and B are put side by side: either (i) PARALLEL different-mechanism alternatives with overlapping scope (both model the same phenomenon, different assumptions), or (ii) THEORY-vs-EXPERIMENT / prediction-vs-observation validation ('data compared with predictions', 'simulations agree with experiments', 'in contrast with'), or (iii) equivalence/contrast of formulations ('equivalent', 'the same as', 'rather than'). NOT improves (neither fixes the other's limitation), NOT extends (neither generalizes the other).

replaces.semantic_boundary: X SUBSTITUTES Y outright (X is used INSTEAD of Y; Y is retired). NOT improves (replaces = Y is gone, improves = Y still used + X better).

adapts.description: X adapts Y to a new scenario
adapts.semantic_boundary: X PORTS Y to a NEW scenario/regime/domain Y wasn't designed for (adaptation of Y's mechanism). NOT extends (adapts = new scenario, extends = broader scope within same setting).

background.semantic_boundary: X cites Y as MOTIVATION/prior context only (Y inspired X but X is NOT a direct technical extension/inheritance of Y). NOT extends (no direct technical lineage), NOT improves (no limitation fix).

closer_to.description: X is closer to Y than to other alternatives (X is more similar to Y than to other approaches, indicating a degree of methodological proximity).
closer_to.semantic_boundary: Use when one method is explicitly positioned as more similar or proximal to another than to alternatives; not for general comparison, ranking, or shared-feature listing.

validates_with.description: X is validated/verified by comparison with Y (X's predictions or results are checked against Y, which could be experimental data or another theory).
validates_with.semantic_boundary: Use when one method’s output is explicitly checked against another method’s output or data; not for mere comparison, co-use, or one method generating the other.

contrasts_with.description: X contrasts with Y in terms of scope, assumptions, or applicability (X and Y have different strengths/weaknesses, often complementary).
contrasts_with.semantic_boundary: Use when two methods are explicitly compared as alternatives with trade-offs; NOT for simple co-occurrence, sequential use, or one method merely improving another.

agrees_with.description: X agrees with / is consistent with Y (X's predictions or values match Y's within some tolerance, often used for theory-theory or theory-experiment agreement).
agrees_with.semantic_boundary: agrees_with applies when X and Y are explicitly compared for consistency, NOT when one causes, explains, or is merely associated with the other.

deviates_from.description: X deviates from / differs from Y (X's predictions or values diverge from Y's, often with a quantified or qualitative difference).
deviates_from.semantic_boundary: Use when X and Y are explicitly compared as divergent, not when one causes, predicts, or merely differs in kind without stated deviation.

compares_within_theory.description: X compares with Y within the same theoretical framework or model, where X and Y are different stress components or predictions from the same theory.
compares_within_theory.semantic_boundary: Applies when two properties are explicitly compared as alternatives or predictions within one theory, not when they are merely co-listed or linked by causal/derivational dependence.

applies_method_to.description: X applies method Y to study/analyze Z (a method is used on a system/material).
applies_method_to.semantic_boundary: Use when a method is explicitly applied to a subject; NOT when the subject is merely described, compared, or co-listed with other things.

discussed_in.description: X is discussed in / presented in Y (a topic is covered in a source or section).
discussed_in.semantic_boundary: Use discussed_in only when the source explicitly presents or covers the topic as its subject; do not use for mere mentions, citations, or co-occurrence in the same text.

analogous_to.description: X is analogous to / similar in nature to Y (X and Y share a qualitative similarity in behavior, mechanism, or form, often noted as a parallel or precedent).
analogous_to.semantic_boundary: Use for qualitative parallels or precedents, NOT for causal, part-whole, or functional dependence relations.

compares_predictions.description: A method's predictions are compared with another method's predictions or with experimental data, often as a function of a parameter.
compares_predictions.semantic_boundary: Applies when predictions from two methods are explicitly compared, not when one method's prediction is merely evaluated against data or when methods are listed without comparison.

predicts.description: X (a theory/method) predicts / yields values of Y (a property or quantity).
predicts.semantic_boundary: Use when a method/theory explicitly yields or forecasts property values; not for mere association, correlation, or co-occurrence of properties.

captures_phenomenon.description: X (a model/method/theory) captures/describes/reproduces Y (a phenomenon or behavior), indicating that X successfully represents or accounts for Y's features.
captures_phenomenon.semantic_boundary: Use when a method/model explicitly explains or reproduces a phenomenon’s behavior; NOT for mere correlation, prediction, or listing of features.

compares_numeric_to_property.description: A numeric value is compared to a property value (e.g., '9.13 is 20% less than the yield torque observed by...'). This is a comparison between a specific numeric measurement and a property's value, distinct from comparing two methods or two properties.
compares_numeric_to_property.semantic_boundary: Use when a number is explicitly compared to a property’s value, not when comparing two properties or two methods.

compares_model_to_data.description: A model's simulation results are compared to experimental data (e.g., 'Steady-state simulation results obtained using the NGF model... are included in Figs. 3 and 4'). This is a comparison between a model's output and data, distinct from comparing two methods or two properties.
compares_model_to_data.semantic_boundary: Applies when a model’s simulated output is explicitly compared to experimental data, not when comparing two methods, two properties, or two models’ outputs.

approximates.description: X approximates Y (X is a simplified or idealized version of Y, used as a stand-in for modeling purposes).
approximates.semantic_boundary: Use for simplified stand-ins in modeling, not for exact equality, representation, or causal claims.

regime_transition.description: X transitions to / is characterized by Y, where X and Y are distinct regimes or states of a system, and the transition between them is governed by a parameter or condition.
regime_transition.semantic_boundary: Use when a system changes from one regime to another due to a condition; NOT for static co-existence, mere correlation, or a single regime’s properties.

rationalizes.description: X (a theory, model, or explanation) rationalizes / provides a coherent account of Y (experimental observations or data), indicating that X offers a conceptual framework that makes sense of Y.
rationalizes.semantic_boundary: Use only when a method explicitly explains or makes sense of observed data; not for mere correlation, prediction, or when the method is just applied without providing a rationale.

predicts_phenomenon.description: X (a theory/method) predicts / yields values or behaviors of Y (a phenomenon), where the prediction concerns the phenomenon's occurrence or characteristics.
predicts_phenomenon.semantic_boundary: Predicts applies when a method/theory yields a phenomenon’s values or behavior; NOT when it merely explains, describes, or co-occurs with it.

studies_phenomenon.description: X (a method or investigation approach) studies/analyzes Y (a phenomenon or system), where X is the investigative tool and Y is the subject of investigation.
studies_phenomenon.semantic_boundary: Use when X is an investigative tool or method actively examining Y, not when X merely describes, causes, or co-occurs with Y.

effectively_becomes.description: X effectively becomes Y, where X is a physical entity or condition that takes on the characteristics of Y due to some process or interaction.
effectively_becomes.semantic_boundary: Applies when X transforms into Y via a process or interaction, NOT when X merely has Y as an attribute, property, or static state.

phase_sequence.description: One phase or regime sequentially follows another in a process (e.g., compaction phase followed by recovery phase).
phase_sequence.semantic_boundary: phase_sequence applies when one regime temporally gives way to another in a process, NOT when regimes coexist, overlap, or are merely listed as simultaneous states.

relates_to.description: X is mathematically related to Y via a known relation or formula, where X and Y are quantities or parameters connected by an established equation (e.g., Einstein relation connecting mean square displacement to diffusion coefficient).
relates_to.semantic_boundary: Use for explicit equations or formulas linking quantities; NOT for mere co-occurrence, correlation, or causal claims without a stated mathematical relation.

alternative_expression.description: X can be expressed in an alternative form Y, where X and Y are equivalent formulations of the same quantity or concept.
alternative_expression.semantic_boundary: Use for equivalent reformulations of the same quantity or concept, not for causal, definitional, or part-whole relations.

propagates_along.description: X (a curve, wave, or entity) propagates along or through Y (a medium or region), with a specified direction or condition.
propagates_along.semantic_boundary: Use when a thing moves or spreads through a medium over time; not for static containment, mere co-occurrence, or causal influence without propagation.

generates.description: One entity (e.g., a moving point) generates or produces another entity (e.g., a non-uniform section of a shock) as a consequence of its motion or behavior (e.g., 'the triple-point moves upstream... as it generates the non-uniform section of the third shock'). This is a causal production relation, distinct from influences (which is a functional dependence between quantities) and from composed_of (structural parts).
generates.semantic_boundary: Use generates only when one phenomenon causally produces another through motion or behavior, not for mere influence, co-occurrence, or part-whole composition.
